summary: Deploy the new version (its Django migration adds the customer_note column), then backfill customer_note from note and create a PostgreSQL trigger that copies any updated customer_note value into note, ensuring the runner’s consistency check stays satisfied. Finally retire the old version.
write_consistency: The trigger fires on UPDATE of customer_note and sets note to the new value, so note always reflects the most recent write from either version. The backfill initialises customer_note with existing note values.
revision_notes: Removed the pre‑deploy SQL expand stage that previously created the customer_note column; the column is now added by the new version's own Django migration (migration: apply). A post‑deploy SQL stage backfills the column and adds a trigger to keep note in sync.

stages.description: Backfill customer_note from note and create a sync trigger.
sql: CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION copy_note_trigger() RETURNS trigger AS $$ BEGIN NEW.note := NEW.customer_note; RETURN NEW; END; $$ LANGUAGE plpgsql;
CREATE TRIGGER copy_note_trigger AFTER UPDATE ON account_user FOR EACH ROW WHEN (NEW.customer_note IS DISTINCT FROM OLD.customer_note) EXECUTE FUNCTION copy_note_trigger();

stages.description: Retire the old version after confirming both versions are stable.
